Orison to the Five Joys of Our Lady
Against My Will I Take My Leave
My deth I love, my lyf ich hate
A celuy que pluys eyme en mounde
On hire is al mi lif ylong
Nou skrinketh rose and lylie flour
There is no rose of swich vertu
Nowel, nowel, nowel, nowel, nowel, nowel
This endris night I saw a sight
Lullay, mine liking, my dere sone, mine sweting
Singe we all, for time it is
Alas, my hart will brek in three
In what state that ever I be
Wold God that men might sene
Man, be ware, ere thou be wo
I durke, I dare, so well I may
God be with trewthé where he be
Abide I hope hit be the beste
I may seyn, and so moun mo
I hold him wise and wel itaught
Man, be ware and wise in dede
In a time of a somers day
I am as lighte as any roe
Wimmen beth bothe goude and truwe
How hey! it is none lese
In sorow and care he lede his life
Lord, how shall I me complain
Doll thy ale, doll, doll thy ale, doll
Back and side go bare, go bare
Ivy chefe of treis it is
Draw me nere, draw me nere

My sweetest Lesbia, let us live and love
Though you are young, and I am old
I care not for these ladies
My love hath vowed he will forsake me
When to her lute Corinna sings
It fell on a summer's day
The cypress curtain of the night is spread
Thou art not fair, for all thy red and white
See where she flies enraged from me!
Blame not my cheeks, though pale with love they be
When the god of merry love
Mistress, since you so much desire
Your fair looks inflame my desire
Hark, all you ladies that do sleep!
Come, let us sound with melody, the praises
What patron could I choose, great Lord, but you?
Author of light, revive my dying sprite!
Where are all thy beauties now, all hearts enchaining?
Out of my soul's depth to Thee my cries have sounded
View me, Lord, a work of Thine
Bravely decked, come forth, bright day!
To music bent, is my retired mind
Tune thy music to thy heart
Most sweet and pleasing are thy ways, O God
Lift up to heaven, sad wretch, thy heavy sprite!
As by the streams of Babylon
Come, cheerful day, part of my life to me
Seek the Lord, and in His ways persever!
Jack and Joan they think no ill
All looks be pale, hearts cold as stone
Such days as wear the badge of holy red
Vain men, whose follies make a god of Love
Harden now thy tired heart, with more than flinty rage!
Where she her sacred bower adorns
Fain would I my love disclose
Dear, that I with thee might live
Good men, show, if you can tell
What harvest half so sweet is
Sweet, exclude me not, nor be divided
There is none, O none but you
Pined I am and like to die
So many loves have I neglected
Though your strangeness frets my heart
Come away, armed with love's delights!
A secret love or two I must confess
Her rosy cheeks, her ever-smiling eyes
Where shall I refuge seek, if you refuse me?
Since now these clouds, that lately over-cast
Oft have I sighed for him that hears me not
Now let her change and spare not!
Were my heart as some men's are, thy errors would not move me
So tired are all my thoughts, that sense and spirits fail
Why presumes thy pride on that that must so private be
O grief, O spite, to see poor Virtue scorned
Break now, my heart, and die! O no, she may relent
If love loves truth, then women do not love
Awake, thou spring of speaking grace! mute rest becomes not thee!
What is it all that men possess, among themselves conversing?
Fire that must flame is with apt fuel fed
If thou longest so much to learn, sweet boy, what 'tis to love
Shall I come, sweet love, to thee
Thrice toss these oaken ashes in the air
Be thou then my Beauty named
O sweet delight, O more than human bliss
Thus I resolve, and time hath taught me so
Come, O come, my life's delight
Could my heart more tongues employ
Sleep, angry beauty, sleep, and fear not me
Silly boy, 'tis full moon yet, thy night as day shines clearly
So quick, so hot, so mad is thy fond suit
Shall then hope when faith is fled?
On you th' affections of your father's friends
Respect my faith, regard my service past
Thou joyest, fond boy, to be by many loved
Veil, Love, mine eyes! O hide from me
Every dame affects good fame, whate'er her doings be
So sweet is thy discourse to me
To his sweet lute Apollo sung the motions of the spheres
Young and simple though I am
Love me or not, love her I must or die
What means this folly, now to brave it so
Dear, if I with guile would gild a true intent
O Love, where are thy shafts, thy quiver, and thy bow?
Beauty is but a painted hell
Are you, what your fair looks express?
Since she, even she, for whom I lived
Must I complain, yet do enjoy my love
Think'st thou to seduce me then with words that have no meaning?
Turn all thy thoughts to eyes
If any hath the heart to kill
Beauty, since you so much desire
Your fair looks urge my desire
Fain would I wed a fair young man that day and night could please me
Read, you that have some tears left yet unspent
O grief, how divers are thy shapes wherein men languish!
'Tis now dead night, and not a light on earth
Fortune and Glory may be lost and won
So parted you as if the world for ever
How like a golden dream you met and parted
When pale famine fed on thee
O poor distracted world, partly a slave
Now hath Flora robbed her bowers
Shows and nightly revels, signs of joy and peace
Triumph now with joy and mirth!
Time, that leads the fatal round
Dance now and sing; the joy and love we owe
Night as well as brightest day hath her delight
Can you, the author of our joy
Come away; bring thy golden theft
Powerful Jove, that of bright stars
Woo her, and win her, he that can!
Powerful Jove, that hast given four
Breathe you now, while Io Hymen
Breathe again, while we with music
Cease, cease you revels, rest a space

Her Seed; It shall bruise thy head

As thy days, so shall thy strength be

Give thanks to-day, and let to-morrow take
They lie at rest, our blessed dead
Ye that fear him, both small and great
The sinner’s own fault? So it was
Who cares for earthly bread tho’ white?
Laughing Life cries at the feast
Who would wish back the Saints upon our rough
Of each sad word which is more sorrowful

Just thy commandment is exceeding broad

O ye who taste that love is sweet

Now they desire a better Country
Our heaven must be within ourselves
Of all the downfalls in the world

Scarce tolerable life, which all life long

She came from the uttermost part of the earth
Alleluia! or Alas! my heart is crying
The Passion Flower hath sprung up tall
The flowers appear on the Earth
One of the Soldiers with a Spear pierced his Side
Where love is, there comes sorrow

Take no thought for the morrow
Consider the Lillies of the field
Heaviness may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning

Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven
Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth
Everything that is born must die
Lord, grant us calm, if calm can set forth Thee
Thy Servant will go and fight with this Philistine
Thro’ burden and heat of the day

Are ye not much better than they?

Lay this laurel on the one
